header_notes: Discovery pass complete: 2026-10-23 09:40 EDT. All rigs (1 to 10, the ceremony dry-run, assumption-gap, combinatorial and metamorphic) are REPORTED and their findings are folded into this file. Next step is the fix phase.

Rig 10 PASSED: the live Base set of Oct 22 is byte-identical to what was tested (live 350 of 350 checks PASS, dry-run 349 of 349, 0 mismatches, 0 incomplete). So every finding tagged LIVE and CONFIRMED below is present in the deployed contracts (HH-008 is app code, not a contract).

Ceremony dry-run gas: every one of the 72 transactions was sent at the 16,777,216 gas cap (Base per-transaction maximum, EIP-7825). Actual use was 30,295 to 4,247,636 per transaction (109,844,802 total), so none came near the cap.
Fix-phase note: rigs/hardhat also adds an npm script 'ceremony:dryrun' to base-contracts/package.json. That is outside testing-rigs/ and was not brought to main.

Rigs 3 and 8 (fuzz_mutation.json) labelled live/latent against the Oct 21 build 7dee25d with no Stake or Synth. That was wrong: the live Oct 22 set is byte-identical to main b0e38a9 with Stake, Synth and the 15 readers deployed and registered. The recorder relabelled every FZ row by the scope rules below; the "exposure" text inside fuzz_mutation.json is superseded.
class_rule: CONFIRMED VULNERABILITY = reproduced by a PoC; SPEC CONFLICT = code differs from Rev 6/12/13 with no exploit shown; UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION = static or reasoning only; INCOMPLETE TESTING = a tool could not finish, which is not evidence of safety. Rigs that already classify their findings keep their class; assumption-gap findings are classified by this rule.
scope_rule: LIVE (Base set) = reachable on the live Base set today (Base-only app config, commit 5a21665; only Base ETH has a usable scheduled price). LIVE (ERC-20 path) = in a live Base contract but only reachable once an ERC-20 is priced or locked. LIVE (on-chain; gated only by non-Base prices not yet posted) = the non-Base reader is registered in the live finalized Base Verifier (rig 9 read-only check); the app's Base-only config hides the UI but does not block direct contract calls, so one posted price for that asset opens the path. LATENT (non-Base only) = non-Base path not yet rechecked against the rig 9 correction. N/A (tooling coverage) = tooling coverage, not a code path. N/A (test gap in a LIVE contract) = a mutant or path the test suite does not exercise, in a contract that is deployed in the live Oct 22 set; not a demonstrated exploit.

findings.description: Assumed: The header is part of the source chain's settled (finalized) history, on the named chain Gap: Only keccak(header) == claimed hash, claimed height == header number, and claimed chain id == the reader's own constant. The claimed chain id is the caller's word; an Ethereum header carries no chain id. Nothing ties the header to any real chain. EthereumLockReader (beacon light client) exists but the ceremony registers SimpleEthereumLockReader; the checkers/ finality contracts are never called by any reader. Exploit: Run a local fork, create a real-looking lock, then rewrite header fields (mixHash, parentHash) so the header exists on no chain; the receipt proof still matches its receiptsRoot. Submit with claimed chain id 1. Known Oct 22 finding (non_base_finality_trust_model.test.cjs): about 311 VCLM per forged lock.
findings.damage_potential: Unlimited VCLM mint up to the 500,000,000 hard cap, and CHONX after activation, with no real asset locked. Inflated supply also inflates RAC and stake rewards.

findings.description: Assumed: Prices come from the twice-daily scheduled run; a record is valid until the next run; the poster has no value authority Gap: Only poster identity, runId > last, price > 0. Exploit: A compromised or mistaken poster posts 1000x price and mints from a tiny lock; or posts runId 2^64-1 to freeze prices. PoC: a 0.001 ETH lock minted 31,096 VCLM.

findings.description: The USDC/USDT $0.95 rule is applied at the first Verifier submission, not at lock creation, in both directions. The spec says a stablecoin below $0.95 is unavailable for every new lock, and that an existing lock keeps its creation price. (a) Depeg after the lock: a USDT lock created at $1.00 and first submitted after a run at $0.94 is refused with VF-ORC-005; the fee is kept and no VCLM is issued while the price stays below $0.95. (b) Lock during a depeg: the lock contracts have no $0.95 check, so a USDC_X lock is accepted at $0.94 and the fee taken. The Verifier refuses it while the price is below $0.95, but the refusal leaves the lock unbound, so after a later run at $1.00 it mints at $1.00. This happens even when the record was attempted at creation. Only the app is meant to refuse the lock; a direct contract call skips that.
findings.damage_potential: (b) Buy a depegged USDC/USDT row, lock it, and mint at the recovered price: about 6% more VCLM per dollar at a $0.94 depeg, scaling with depeg depth. (a) Fee paid with no mint during a depeg.
evidence: Part (a): 156 cells DEVIATION:valid_lock_not_minted (stable_above_then_below, VF-ORC-005), Base and Ethereum. Part (b): 308 cells DEVIATION:minted_but_spec_refuses (stable_below_then_above, 154 of them bound, with record_err_A VF-ORC-005 and the record at B succeeding), plus 4 Handshake cells where the lock was accepted, the fee taken and the later band check refused it (DEVIATION:lock_accepted_fee_taken_no_mint). Example: USDC_X lock at $0.94 worth $0.01 minted 0.138 VCLM at the $1.00 run.
findings.related: AG-06 (price bound at first submission); AG-11 (which rows the $0.95 rule catches)

findings.description: A lock that is valid at creation (in band at the creation price, fee already paid to the Dev Fund) becomes unmintable if a price run moves its USD out of band before the first submission. The Verifier re-checks the band at the later price: a Handshake that rises above $0.02 is refused with VF-COM-003, and a standard lock that falls below $0.01 is refused with VF-COM-009. The fee is kept and no VCLM is issued. The spec says a lock keeps its creation price. Root cause is AG-06 (price bound at first submission); AG-16 is the lock-side band gate.
findings.damage_potential: User pays the fee and gets no VCLM for a valid lock. Limited to locks near the band edges and to the fee amount. Principal release at maturity was not tested by this rig.
evidence: 68 cells DEVIATION:valid_lock_not_minted outside the stablecoin classes: TKN price 2 to 1 drops $0.01 and $0.015 standard locks below $0.01 (60 cells, VF-COM-009); ETH price x2 pushes $0.015 and $0.02 Handshakes above $0.02 (4 cells, VF-COM-003); TKN Handshake cases (4 cells, VF-COM-003). All on Base and Ethereum alike. Fee equals the 5% floor and reached the Dev Fund in every one.
findings.related: AG-06 (price bound at first submission is the root cause); AG-16 (lock-side band gate)
